content: The majority of the systems assigned higher scores to sentences with African American names on the tasks of anger, fear, and sadness intensity prediction. On the joy and valence tasks, most submissions tended to assign higher scores to sentences with European American names. These tendencies reflect some common stereotypes that associate African Americans with more negative emotions BIBREF28 .
